title: Learning the chord system from Gene Porter
summary: Saxophonist Gene Porter, newly out of Des Dunes' band, showed him to call chords by number. DeLay says he was among the first New Orleans trumpeters to play by chord system.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: What to think while improvising: wrong notes and being in the moment

blocks.x: So one guy gave me a, I don't know, made me feel changed sort of. I took to this guy, his name was Gene Porter, a saxophone player. Oh, yeah. He had just got out of Des Dune's band. Des Dune had died and he came from, I think he died in Mexico and they came over there and there was a guy by the name of Greg, played trumpet, and this little guy, Henry Halloway, his name is Kildee we call him, I think he's around New Orleans yet. Well they all came over there, oh a lot of musicians, they came over there just to get a workout at the dance hall. And I was amazed by the, about this guy not knowing numbers and having the guys to call the chords. And I talked to him and he told me about it and I just went and flew with the piano, I knew the chords, at least that's the only thing I didn't know was the foundation, not articulation, I never was much. And I followed it from there and I began playing what you call a chord system. And incidentally, hate to put it that way, but I think I was about the first trumpet player to actually start to play a chord system around New Orleans. Actually knowing that I mean.
Yeah knowing what chord you were playing.
